clue.text: A rating, as it turns out, one born late in the year

definitions.text: one born late in the year

indicators.note: how something turns out is how it ends up arranged, so the eleven letters of the fodder are reworked

explanation.surface: A sailor, as it happens, has a birthday towards the end of the year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rating' looks like the naval rank, but A RATING AS IT is simply the letter pool for 'turns out'.
explanation.definitionFit: The zodiac sign Sagittarius covers late November to late December, so its people have birthdays near year's end.

clue.text: Work for press, taking public transport to north

indicators.note: in a down entry, going to north means the letters run upwards, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: a bus is public transport

explanation.surface: A journalist commutes northwards on the bus to work on a newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: A sub-editor prepares copy for the printing press; to sub is that job.

clue.text: Relish time supporting America in game

indicators.note: the pieces sit in the word for the game, so that word is split around them

parts.note: Go is the Japanese board game

indicators.note: in a down entry a supporting piece sits beneath the other one

parts.note: US is America

explanation.surface: Someone enjoys time spent backing America at a sporting fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish as a noun means hearty enjoyment, the same as zest or enthusiasm.

clue.text: Russian writer's means to get rid of old model

indicators.note: getting rid of something drops it, so the letter for old leaves the word for means

parts.note: tools are means to an end, instruments
a toy can be a model, as in a toy car or toy train

explanation.surface: A Russian author's method for disposing of an outdated model.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's after 'writer' stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy wrote War and Peace and Anna Karenina, a giant of Russian literature.

clue.text: Last aria Rameau finally composed for land down under

indicators.note: composing puts things together in order, so these letters are arranged afresh
finally points at the closing letter of the composer's name

explanation.surface: The French composer Rameau finally wrote a last aria for Australia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composed' suits the musical surface but is the anagram signal: LAST ARIA plus U, the last letter of Rameau, is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Down Under is the well-known nickname for the Antipodes, particularly the continent-country beneath Asia.

clue.text: Lives with girl? That's the problem!

parts.note: lives can mean is, exists
Sue is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone cohabiting with a girlfriend: that's the trouble!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lives with' reads as sharing a home; really IS is placed with SUE.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a matter of contention or a difficulty, as in 'that's the issue here'.

clue.text: Particle identified by Greek character, an Athenian demagogue

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
Cleon was a populist leader of Athens during the Peloponnesian War

explanation.surface: A small item linked to a Greek figure and an Athenian rabble-rouser.
explanation.definitionFit: A proton or neutron in an atom's nucleus is collectively called this kind of particle.

clue.text: Altercation in bank?

definitions.meaning: a bank of seats or switches is a line of them

explanation.surface: A dispute breaks out at the bank.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a heated quarrel and a line of things, as a bank of keys is.

clue.text: Contrite theatre worker touring hospital department

indicators.note: touring goes all round something, so the theatre and worker pair wraps the department

parts.note: rep is repertory theatre
an ant is the classic worker in crosswords
ENT is ear, nose and throat, a hospital department

explanation.surface: A stagehand on a tour of a hospital ward feels sorry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'theatre worker' reads as one stagehand, but the two words are separate pieces split apart by the hospital department.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrite and the answer both describe someone sorry for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Preacher entertaining northern duke with beer and cheese

indicators.note: entertaining a guest means holding them inside, so the preacher's name contains the letter

parts.note: John Wesley was the founding preacher of Methodism
ale is beer

explanation.surface: A preacher hosts a northern duke with a pint and some cheese.
explanation.definitionFit: This crumbly Yorkshire cheese is named after the dale where it is made.

clue.text: Lethal serpents a reclusive saint chances heading off

parts.note: St Basil the Great lived for a time as a hermit and founded monastic rule

indicators.note: with its heading off a word loses its first letter

parts.note: risks are chances

explanation.surface: A hermit saint takes chances near deadly snakes.
explanation.walkthrough: RISKS with its first letter cut gives ISKS.
explanation.definitionFit: The basilisk of legend is a serpent king whose gaze or breath kills.

clue.text: Fattened fowl a gang leader left unfinished

indicators.note: something left unfinished lacks its end, so the final letter goes

parts.note: Al Capone led the Chicago Outfit gang

explanation.surface: A mobster abandons a plump chicken half-eaten.
explanation.definitionFit: A capon is a castrated cockerel fattened for the table.

clue.text: Small farmer more frequently pursuing credit

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so this piece comes after the credit abbreviation

parts.note: ofter is an old comparative of often

explanation.surface: A smallholder chasing credit more and more often.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scotland a croft is a small rented farm, and its tenant works a smallholding.

clue.text: Blunt old PM collecting key cake ingredient

indicators.note: collecting something takes it in, so the word for blunt holds the key

parts.note: blunt means frank, candid
E is a musical key
Robert Peel was a 19th-century British prime minister

explanation.surface: A frank former prime minister picks up a key ingredient for a cake.
explanation.definitionFit: Sugared citrus rind is chopped into fruitcakes and Christmas cakes.

clue.text: Endless delay regularly besetting seabird by lake

indicators.note: besetting surrounds on all sides, so the alternate letters go round the bird
regularly takes every other letter, here the second and fourth of delay

parts.note: a tern is a seabird

explanation.surface: Constant hold-ups harass a seabird beside the lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' picks E and A from 'delay'; these surround TERN.
explanation.definitionFit: Something everlasting has no end, which is what endless says.

clue.text: Single doctor in US city, one opposing local development

indicators.note: the pieces are placed in the city abbreviation, which splits around them

parts.note: NY is New York
I, the Roman numeral one, is single
MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree

explanation.surface: An unmarried doctor in a US city fights a new building nearby.
explanation.definitionFit: The acronym 'not in my back yard' labels a resident who objects to building near home.

clue.text: Fantasist reportedly confined and mollified

indicators.note: reportedly says the name is to be taken as heard, not as spelt

parts.note: Walter Mitty is the daydreaming fantasist of James Thurber's story
gated means confined, as a pupil kept in school as punishment

explanation.surface: A daydreamer, so they say, was locked up and calmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gated' is a British school term for being confined to the premises.
explanation.definitionFit: Mollified and the answer both mean softened or made less severe.

clue.text: Famous lad with energy for exercising

indicators.note: exercising puts things through their paces, working the letters into new positions

explanation.surface: A boy known for his energy at physical training.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone celebrated enough to be the stuff of legend is very well known.

clue.text: Two chaps providing capital cover in Kyle of Localsh?

definitions.text: capital cover in Kyle of Localsh?

parts.note: two chaps: the first of the pair is Glen, a man's name
the second of the two chaps is Garry, another man's name

explanation.surface: Two men supply headgear in a Scottish Highland village.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' means the head, so 'capital cover' is a hat; Kyle of Lochalsh (spelt 'Localsh' here) is a Highland town, making it Scottish headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: This brimless boat-shaped Scottish cap is worn with Highland dress.

clue.text: Lacking will to reject place in fashionable gallery?

indicators.note: the reversed word goes in between the other two pieces

parts.note: in means fashionable
the Tate is the London art gallery

indicators.note: rejecting turns something back, so the word for place reads in reverse

parts.note: to set is to place

explanation.surface: Without the resolve to turn down a spot in a trendy art gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies with no valid will is said to have died this way.

clue.text: Agitate about rider's first piece of tack

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the phrase for agitate goes round the letter

parts.note: to stir up is to agitate

indicators.note: first points at the opening letter of rider's

explanation.surface: Stirring up trouble around a rider's first bit of horse gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tack' is riding equipment such as saddle and bridle.
explanation.definitionFit: Tack is a horse's harness, and the foot-rest hung from a saddle is part of it.

clue.text: Fish touristy restaurants originally included in meal?

indicators.note: the picked letters go inside the word for meal

parts.note: tea is an early-evening meal in Britain

indicators.note: originally takes the opening letter of each of the two words

explanation.surface: Seafood on the menu at tourist restaurants as part of a set meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A small brightly coloured tropical freshwater fish popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Travel agency giving shelter to a crested African bird

indicators.note: sheltering something means holding it within, so the pair wraps the letter

parts.note: to tour is to travel
CO, company, is a business or agency

explanation.surface: A tour company hides a crested bird from Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Turacos are brightly coloured crested birds of sub-Saharan Africa.

clue.text: Shark that's spotted female is hot on trail

indicators.note: in an across entry 'on' means placed after, so those letters follow the trail word

parts.note: to dog is to trail or follow
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on a tap

explanation.surface: A shark is seen; a woman is hot on its trail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spotted' reads as 'seen' but the lesser spotted variety is a shark with a dotted skin.
explanation.definitionFit: The lesser spotted species is a small British shark with dappled skin.

clue.text: Greek poet's house overlooking sea at Boulogne

indicators.note: in a down entry overlooking means sitting above, so the house letters come first

parts.note: mer is French for sea, as spoken in Boulogne

explanation.surface: A Greek poet's villa looks out over the sea at a French port.
explanation.definitionFit: The Iliad and the Odyssey are traditionally credited to this ancient Greek.

clue.text: Leave university with a revolutionary painting technique

parts.note: to go is to leave
Che Guevara is the crossword's stock revolutionary

explanation.surface: Someone drops out of university alongside a radical painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Opaque watercolour, thicker than ordinary watercolour, is the medium named here.

clue.text: City overwhelmed by Conservative member's vice

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means smothered, so the city is enclosed by the other pieces

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: A city overpowered by a Tory MP's wickedness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vice' looks like the moral failing; here it is the workshop tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A vice is a tool that grips work, much as a clamp holds things tight.

clue.text: Woman abandoning horse in compound

indicators.note: abandoning means leaving behind, so the letter for horse drops out

parts.note: Hester is a woman's name
H is slang for heroin, known as horse

explanation.surface: A woman leaves her horse in a farm enclosure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horse' is drug slang for heroin, abbreviated H; 'compound' is the chemical sense, not a yard.
explanation.definitionFit: An organic chemical compound formed from an acid and an alcohol.

clue.text: Preserve sheep brought back by young chap in West

indicators.note: by means next to, placing the two pieces side by side
brought back means turned round, so the word for sheep is read in reverse

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep

indicators.note: the young man goes inside the actress's first name

parts.note: Mae West was the Hollywood actress
a lad is a young chap

explanation.surface: A sheep is driven home by a young farmhand out West.
explanation.definitionFit: Orange jam, a preserve of citrus fruit, is the breakfast spread meant.

clue.text: Blunder made by English kings

parts.note: R, rex, stands for king, so two kings give RR

explanation.surface: A mistake made by the English monarchs.
explanation.definitionFit: To blunder is to make a mistake, which is the verb's sense.

clue.text: Went in front, having source of light

definitions.meaning: describing a lamp fitted with a light-emitting diode

explanation.surface: Someone took the lead, carrying a lamp.
explanation.definitionFit: The past tense of lead, and the light-emitting diode used as an adjective for lamps.

clue.text: Do gymnastics, taken in by pathetic spoilsport

parts.note: a do is a party

indicators.note: taken in by means enclosed, so the gymnastics letters sit inside the word for pathetic

parts.note: poor means pathetic, feeble
PE, physical education, covers gymnastics

explanation.surface: Doing gymnastics, fooled by a pitiful killjoy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' looks like a verb but is the noun for a celebration.
explanation.definitionFit: A killjoy who dampens everyone's fun is exactly this kind of person.
